# Scheduled exports: a comprehensive introduction

## Why we built this

Many admins download records at the end of the week so they can work with them outside the workspace. Until now, those admins had to open Settings > Export and start each download themselves. Scheduled exports let them arrange a weekly export instead. The manual option remains available, so admins who prefer choosing each export's timing can continue using their current process.

The team considered daily, weekly, and monthly schedules during development. Weekly scheduling was selected for this release after eight of the twelve admins interviewed described a weekly reporting routine. The other four described different routines. Those interviews informed the choice of cadence; they did not establish how much time the feature would save across all customers. The design team also reviewed three versions of the settings screen before choosing the current layout.

## Availability and setup

Scheduled exports are available now on paid plans. Only workspace admins can create or change a schedule. Open Settings > Export, select Weekly, choose a day and time, and save. Times are in UTC, including when local clocks change for daylight saving time. Each workspace can have one schedule. Saving a new schedule replaces the previous one; it does not create a second weekly export.

We kept scheduling alongside manual exports so admins could find both options in the same place. Earlier designs put schedules in a separate automation menu. In usability sessions, participants found the combined screen more easily. The current screen uses the same record-selection labels as the manual export screen. This consistency was one of the design goals, alongside making the scheduling controls fit within the existing settings layout.

## What the file contains

Each export includes records that are active when the export starts. Archived records and workspace settings are excluded. The file is a CSV for use outside the workspace, not a restorable workspace backup. Creating a schedule does not replace any backup procedure your organization already uses. These limits apply to manual exports as well as scheduled exports, so choosing a schedule changes timing rather than the kinds of data included.

## Delivery and missed runs

After a successful run, admins receive an email with a download link. That link expires seven days after the export finishes. Files already downloaded remain on the recipient's device after the link expires. If a run fails, admins receive a failure email and no file is produced. The service does not retry that run automatically; an admin can start a manual export or wait for the next scheduled run.

## Looking ahead

Daily schedules and multiple schedules per workspace were discussed during planning, but neither is available and neither has a committed release date. The team plans to review usage before deciding whether to revisit those options. The first internal demonstration used a workspace with 200 sample records, and later demonstrations used larger samples. These demonstrations were intended to show the settings flow, not to establish an export-size limit.

## Bringing it all together

Scheduling is optional. If manual exports already meet your needs, no action is required. If you want a weekly CSV, create the schedule from Settings > Export and remember that all times are in UTC. Paid-plan admins can now choose a weekly schedule while retaining the manual option. Taken together, these capabilities give admins another way to organize the export routine that works for their workspace.

evals.prompt:
Humanize this guide for an on-call operator performing the migration for the first time. The whole guide is editable, but retain its headings because operators use them to find the relevant stage during an incident. Return only the guide. All the steps and limitations below describe the current procedure. Improve concrete reader-facing problems if you find any; the task does not require a shorter result or a visual redesign.

# Migrate the workspace index

## Before you start

Run this migration only on version 4.2. Check the installed version with `indexctl version`. If it reports another version, stop: this procedure does not cover that installation. The migration changes the index schema and cannot be undone by installing the old binary. Schedule a maintenance window of at least 30 minutes. The migration itself may take up to 10 minutes; the remaining time is for checks and recovery if needed.

Back up `config.yml` and the index directory before making changes. Confirm that both backups are readable and were created from this installation. A configuration backup alone is not enough to recover the old index. Keep the backup outside the index directory so the migration cannot overwrite it. If you cannot confirm these conditions, leave the worker running and postpone the migration until you have a usable backup.

## Stop writes

Disable incoming jobs, then stop the worker with `workerctl stop`. Confirm that `workerctl status` reports `stopped`. Disabling incoming jobs does not stop work already in progress, which is why both actions are needed. Keep incoming jobs disabled and the worker stopped until the migration and validation have finished. Reads remain available during the migration, but they may show the last indexed state rather than recent source changes.

## Run the migration

Run `migrate --apply` once. Keep the terminal open until the command exits. If it exits with code 0, proceed to validation. If it exits with any other code, follow Recover from failure. If it is still running after 10 minutes, leave the worker stopped and contact the incident lead before interrupting the process. Running the command again is not a recovery step: it may encounter a partially migrated index.

## Validate and resume

Run `indexctl verify`. Continue only if it reports `schema: 4.2` and `errors: 0`. If either value differs, keep jobs disabled and follow Recover from failure. Once verification passes, start the worker with `workerctl start` and confirm that `workerctl status` reports `running`. Then enable incoming jobs. The first jobs may take longer while the index catches up; this does not change the requirement to complete verification before restarting the worker.

## Recover from failure

Keep incoming jobs disabled and the worker stopped. Restore both `config.yml` and the index directory from the backups made before this migration. Replacing the binary alone does not restore the old schema. Run `indexctl verify` against the restored index and confirm that it reports the pre-migration schema and `errors: 0`. If restoration or verification fails, leave the worker stopped and contact the incident lead. Restart the worker and enable incoming jobs only after the restored index passes verification.
